featured_reviews.review_text: It is one of the oldest book stores in Mumbai. They have all of engineering, medical, pharmacy, law, reference, competitive exam books. It's a one stop shop for all of your semester book needs right from the previous year question papers to your desired references and much more. They accept paytm, gpay, and online transfers not to mention cash payments. The shop is located in the heart of Dadar and its easy to locate.

featured_reviews.review_text: This place is truly a hidden gem. In a world where kids are glued to screens, you really need something more engaging than screens to grab their attention and this place has it..... Books! Not just any books; curated, colorful, engaging, "based on real life experiences" books. We were greeted by their very passionate staff and the owner Sangeeta who were excited to see us. I learnt more about storytelling in 5 minutes with Sangeeta than I did in my life. We thought we would buy just a couple of books and leave but after we entered and saw their collection, we left with 15 books (and we stopped coz our baggage allowance on our flight back home wouldn't allow more..lol). Can't wait to be back here soon.

The Bench, the Bar and the Bizarre

If you think the law is always solemn and predictable, this book politely disagrees—and then proves it with style. The Bench, the Bar and the Bizarre takes you into the lesser-seen corners of the legal world, where logic sometimes takes a coffee break and reality feels stranger than fiction.

Through a series of real-life courtroom episodes, Tushar Mehta presents a fascinating blend of wit, absurdity, and insight. From unconventional judicial behavior to cases that stretch imagination, the book captures the unpredictable human side of law.

Law is often seen as stern, structured, and serious—but this book flips the courtroom script. The Lawful and the Awful is a refreshing dive into the quirky, human, and sometimes bizarre side of the legal world.

Drawing from real courtroom episodes across jurisdictions, Tushar Mehta blends wit, sarcasm, and sharp observation to narrate stories where law meets personality—and sometimes loses the plot. For lawyers and law students, this is not just philosophy—it is the foundation behind many principles that courts interpret and apply.
